summary: All 60 findings verified at their evidence: 55 confirmed (6 high, 23 medium, 26 low) and 5 rejected (/18, /19, /21, /22 medium; /38 low). All six high findings hold: the queue's parent-only merge of Part IIs can defer RealSurfacePeriodIndex's suppliers (/1); route 1 creates stage cycles, SF.2↔MC.2 and SF.2↔topology Part II, but the claimed SF.3 cycle is not forced (/2, narrowed); item 141's Witt statement is circular for Proposition 4.2 (/3); items 75/78 drop H¹(R, A|_R) = 0, with the plane-quartic counterexample re-derived (/4); Proposition 6.6's transport step is a real gap needing a pair trivialisation, not plain Ehresmann (/5); item 107's F₂² stalks are Z/4 when 4 ∤ n (/6, arguably medium). Rejections: /18, because ShimuraData:D3 already plans the VHS carrier, so item 151 must stay 'planned', and the D3 versus HodgeStructuresPartII ownership predates this paper and is for the merged design job; /19, because the queue merges all HodgeStructures Part IIs into one design job told to merge overlaps, and the residual naming issue is /1; /21, backwards, because AdicSpacesPartII's F0 node imports Serre vanishing from R09.1 and requests it there; /22, because no other extraction plans integral weak Lefschetz or Andreotti–Frankel (BW20's items are equivariant and use étale Artin vanishing); /38, because the errata record's E13 (confirmed) already requires avoiding zeros and poles, and the residue is folded into /8. Scope corrections the fixer must follow: /2 read together with /24 (the topology Part II imports SF.2's equivariant carriers but not the SF comparison); /4 (Proposition 6.6's very ample A is a different bundle from Proposition 5.5's); /5 (a Thom-isotopy-type pair trivialisation as a cited input); /15 (the Artin comparison goes to Landesman–Litt's owner, IG.0/IG.1, not SF.2); /31 and /33 (cite existing BW20 and CS24 items rather than re-adding them); /53 (the vanishing lemma is root-namespace isZero_groupCohomology_succ_of_subsingleton); /55 (the analytic carrier is the upstream ComplexComparison PR196, not ComplexComparisonPartII:C0). Verdict changes on existing reviews (E3, E13, E19) and the make_queue/REGISTER tooling changes go to the maintainer as notes, not fixer edits.

Read the proof of Proposition 4.2 (published p. 80; TeX identical). For Γ ≅ P^1_R exceptional, the paper picks Γ' meeting Γ transversally at a real point x and meeting T_U. It then knows only 'p*α|_y = 0 for y in Γ'(R) general', and concludes by Witt [Satz 22] that p*α|_{R(Γ')} = 0, hence the residue at x vanishes. That residue 'coincides with the restriction of res_Γ(α) at x'. Item 141 states Witt only for a class 'unramified and trivial at every real point'. Applied to Γ', unramifiedness at x is exactly res_Γ(α)|_x = 0, the conclusion being proved. Γ' may also meet other ramification curves. So item 141 as stated cannot discharge the step, and its 'extends by local constancy' remark fails across ramification points. I checked the mathematics of the proposed restatement. Br(R(C)) is killed by 2 (cores∘res through C(C), which has Br = 0). Witt's theorem (a conic over R(C), C a real curve, has a point iff it has one over every real closure of R(C)) gives injectivity of Br(R(C)) -> product over orderings of Br(R). Orderings are centred at points of the smooth projective model's C(R), and the evaluation is locally constant on the unramified real locus. So vanishing at a dense set of unramified real points forces β = 0, and C(R) = ∅ gives Br(R(C)) = 0. Apply it to the normalisation of Γ' (x is a smooth point of Γ' by transversality). I also confirmed that item 141 is on no proof spine: the spine 'Real degree-two sufficiency under uniform evaluation' contains 64 but not 141. Items carry no separate dependency field. Authorised fix. Restate item 141 as in the finding: C a smooth integral real curve (in use, the normalisation of Γ'), β in Br(R(C)) not assumed unramified, vanishing at a dense set of unramified real points (equivalently at every ordering) implies β = 0, and Br(R(C)) = 0 if C(R) = ∅. Add 141 to that proof spine before 64, and have item 64's statement cite it. Severity: the item is false-for-purpose rather than false, so medium would also be defensible. See /50 for the BW20 witt-curve special case in the same Part II.

Published p. 89 (TeX \label{twistedlb}): 'Let A be an ample line bundle on S, such that H^1(R, A|_R) = 0. Let N := μ*A(2F−2E).' The proof opens 'Condition (iii) follows from our choice of A.' The hypothesis appears nowhere in the extraction. Item 75 takes 'very ample A', and item 78 asserts H^1(R', N|R') = 0 unconditionally. Because P and Q avoid R, R' ≅ R and N|R' = A|R, so item 78 is equivalent to H^1(R, A|R) = 0. I re-derived the counterexample. S = P^2_R, R a smooth real plane quartic (SNC, genus 3), A = O(1) (very ample). Adjunction gives K_R = O_R(4−3) = O_R(1) = A|R, so h^1(R, A|R) = h^0(R, O_R) = 1 ≠ 0. Item 78 as stated is false. Authorised fix. (a) In item 75 replace 'very ample A' by 'A ample on S with H^1(R, A|_R) = 0', as printed. (b) Item 78 states that it follows from this hypothesis. (c) Add that such A exists: for any ample A_0, H^1(R, A_0^m|_R) = 0 for m ≫ 0 by Serre vanishing on the projective curve R (item 138). One correction to the red team's fix: do not write 'Proposition 6.6 chooses A this way'. The proof of Proposition 6.6 (p. 93) invokes Proposition 5.5 only existentially ('we may assume that S carries a line bundle N satisfying Assumption 5.4'). The A it then names is a different, very ample bundle used for L = A^l ⊗ N(−R). The fixer should keep the two bundles apart, for example by naming 5.5's bundle A_0 in item 75. Coordinate with /39: the extraction's label '5.5(iv)' on item 78 is the paper's (iii), and '(i)' on item 75 is the paper's (iv).

Read the end of the proof of Proposition 6.6 (published pp. 94-95; TeX identical) and Proposition 4.5 (p. 84). β in H^2_G(T(C),Z(1)) is only known to induce α_{R(T)}. Such lifts form a coset of 2H^2_G + cl(Pic T), and Proposition 4.5's proof writes β|_{T_U} = p*α̃ + 2ε + cl(φ) with φ in Pic(T_U) arbitrary. The paper then identifies the cohomology of all fibres over Λ(R) through a G-equivariant Ehresmann trivialisation. It finds x with β = 2γ + 2δ + cl(φ_x) in H^2_G(T_x(C),Z(1)) and concludes by (2.17) 'replacing T with T_x'. That needs the transported β to lift α_{T_x}, which is never shown. Changing β by cl(C) (C the special curve) changes the transport by a class that leaves the (1,1) locus (that is the point of items 74 and 86), and the choice of x depends on β. So the step is a genuine gap in the printed argument, not a counterexample. Section 1 avoids it because E2/G2 choose β mod n = p*α̃ with α̃ defined on all of S, and so on the whole family. Section 6 has no analogue. Neither the sourceIssues (E1-E19) nor research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-BENOIST-19.json records it. I checked the repair. φ in Pic(T_U) extends to φ̄ in Pic(T) (T is smooth), and β − cl(φ̄) still lifts α_T, so item 165 ('any integral β') still applies. Its reduction on T_U is exactly p*α̃. If the trivialisation preserves the divisor p^{-1}(R), the reduction of the transported class on T_{x,U} is p_x*α̃. So its image in Br(T_x) restricts to α on T_{x,U}, and Br(T_x) -> Br(R(T_x)) is injective. Authorised fix: (a), (b) and (c) as in the finding. For (b), the fixer must state the relative (pair) trivialisation as an explicit cited input, for example Thom's first isotopy lemma for the family of pairs (T_y, p_y^{-1}(R)), which is equisingular near s because Sing R is fixed and R ∩ D_y moves by transverse points. It must not be presented as plain Ehresmann (item 87). Add a sourceIssue, kind gap, affects 'the proof', known new, with locators Proposition 6.6, pp. 94-95, and Proposition 1.2, p. 71. Extend E2's reason with the second role of the compatible choice. See /23 on the ownership of Ehresmann.

Published p. 100 (TeX, just after Lemma 7.5 'Gzeta'): 'One can compute that its stalks are isomorphic to Z/2 ⊕ Z/2 if 4 | n (resp. to Z/4 if 4 ∤ n), but we will not need this fact.' Item 107 says 'locally constant with F2² stalks' without qualification, which is false for n ≡ 2 mod 4. I recomputed n = 2 from item 106's definition G = coker[(φ_2, 1+σ): ι*Q(1) -> F2 ⊕ (ι*Q(1))^G]. Over a point of the circle no sheet is real, so (p_*Z)_x = Z^2 with σ swapping. Then Q_x = Z^2/diagonal ≅ Z with σ = −1, and Q(1)_x ≅ Z with trivial action, so 1+σ = 2 and φ_2 is reduction mod 2. The cokernel of t ↦ (t mod 2, 2t) in Z/2 ⊕ Z is generated by (0,1), with 2(0,1) = (0,2) ≡ (1,0) ≠ 0 and 4(0,1) = 0, so it is Z/4 and 0 -> Z/2 -> Z/4 -> Z/2 -> 0 is non-split. This matches the paper, and item 156 and G4 already say that no split circle extension follows. The double cover is unaffected: the preimage of 1 under Z/4 -> Z/2 is {1, 3}, of size 2. Authorised fix, as in the finding. Replace the clause by 'locally constant, with stalks (Z/2)^2 if 4 | n and Z/4 otherwise (not used); the fibre over 1 of the quotient map has two elements in either case, so it defines a double cover of S^1'. Restrict unit test 1 to 4 | n, or replace it by the n = 2 computation above. Severity: the clause is not used downstream, so I would rate this medium rather than high, but it is a false statement in an item and must go.

Published p. 92, proof of Lemma 6.4 (TeX \label{lemapprox}, identical). Bröcker gives h_1 'that vanishes at order one along R and H' with no other zeros or poles along S(R). D is the polar divisor of h_1h_2. u = Σu_i² with u_i in H^0(A^{l/2} ⊗ N(−R−D)), viewed in A^{l/2} ⊗ N(−R), so u is a section of A^l ⊗ N²(−2R) vanishing to order 2 along D. Then t := −h_1h_2ru. I recomputed the divisor of t as a section of A^l ⊗ N²(−R): div(h_1h_2) + div(r) + div(u) = (R + H + Z' − D) + R + (2D + Z''), where Z' and Z'' have no real points. That is 2R + H + D + (non-real). So t vanishes doubly along R, {t = 0} is not reduced there, and its real locus is H(R) ∪ R(R) ≠ ι'(S) whenever R(R) ≠ ∅. Local check: R = {y = 0}, H = {x = 0}, h_1 = xy gives t ∝ xy². R(R) ≠ ∅ occurs in the main theorems (R(R) ⊂ Ξ in Proposition 6.6), and there D := {s = 0} with s ≈ a_1s_0 + a_2c, a_2 ≈ t, must have real locus ι(S). So the error propagates into Proposition 6.6's construction. It is not in sourceIssues or the errata record, and I judge it new. Both repairs check out. (1) Take h_1 with divisor H − R near S(R). Bröcker only controls sign changes (the parity of orders along S(R)), and cl_R(H − R) = cl_R(H + R) = 0. With D the part of the polar divisor of h_1h_2 away from R, t is regular with real zero locus exactly H(R), of multiplicity one, and rt = −h_1h_2r²u < 0 on S(R) \ Ξ (h_1h_2 > 0 there, R(R) ⊂ Ξ). (2) Keep h_1, take u_i in H^0(A^{l/2} ⊗ N(−D)) and t := −h_1h_2u/r. Authorised fix, as in the finding. Add a sourceIssue: kind error, affects 'the proof', known new, locator 'Lemma 6.4, proof, published p. 92', printed 'vanishes at order one along R and H'. Give either corrected recipe, and state the chosen recipe in item 83's statement/proof outline. Severity: the lemma itself is true and the repair is local, so medium is right.

Published p. 80: 'If p(Γ) is an irreducible component of R, this follows from [20, 3.3.1]. Otherwise, Γ is an exceptional divisor of the blow-up T -> T̄.' I checked the geometry. Over x in R ∩ D, r(x) = s(x) = 0, so the fibre of T̄ = {rv² = sw²} is the whole P^1 (E1). In local coordinates with r, s transverse parameters, the charts s = rv² and r = sw² are smooth, so T̄ is smooth there and T -> T̄ is an isomorphism near it (the blown-up singular points lie over Sing R only, p. 77). The fibre is therefore a curve of T lying over R, contracted to a point, and not exceptional for T -> T̄. The case split misses it. Item 64 ('exceptional P1 residues') inherits the omission. Items 57 and 182 in the extraction already acknowledge the P^1 fibres. The argument transfers verbatim. These fibres and the exceptional curves over Sing R are pairwise disjoint smooth rational curves (D avoids Sing R), so the ramification locus is smooth and the Gersten step applies. Each fibre is P^1_R over a real point and P^1_C over a non-real closed point, and the Witt test at one real point (corrected item 141, /3) finishes the argument. So Proposition 4.2 is unaffected. Neither record's E1 mentions Proposition 4.2, and the E1 review even says 'nothing downstream breaks because §3.2 onwards works over S* and S⁰', which this proof does not. Authorised fix. Restate item 64 with the three cases (dominating R; exceptional over Sing R; fibres over R ∩ D), same argument for the last two. Add a sourceIssue, kind gap, affects 'the proof', known new, locator 'Proposition 4.2, proof, p. 80', with the printed/correction text of the finding. Add a sentence to E1's reason noting this downstream use. I do not authorise changing E1's 'affects' here. The printed §3.1 sentence 'It is a finite double cover' is itself false, so 'a stated result' is defensible, and any reconciliation belongs to /8.

Read item PAPER-BENOIST-19/118 and its definition item 114 (which says either half 'can be empty') against the proof of Theorem 0.6, printed p. 106 (TeX §8.1). The paper handles S(R) empty first ('If S(R) is empty, per = ind for every alpha by Theorem 0.5. From now on, we suppose that S(R) is nonempty'), and only then writes the H^1 Kummer sequence and the sentence 'there exists a non-zero class delta with [delta]_0 = 0 if and only if one of the two halves of S is empty, and this class is unique'. Item 118 drops that hypothesis. Re-derivation when S(R) is empty: Kummer gives 0 -> R*/R*^2 -> H^1_et(S, Z/2) = H^1_G(S(C), Z/2) -> Pic(S)[2] -> 0 (O(S)* = R* because S is proper and geometrically connected; the comparison is Scheiderer 15.3.1). Pic(S) -> Pic(S_C) is injective by Hilbert 90 (H^1(G, C*) = 0), so Pic(S)[2] lies in Pic(S_C)[2] = Z/2 and contains K_S, which is nonzero. So H^1_G has order 4. Because H^0(S(R), Z/2) = 0, all three nonzero classes (the image omega of -1, and the two lifts of K_S) have [delta]_0 = 0. Both halves are empty, so 'exactly one half is empty' is false, yet nonzero classes exist and are not unique. The item is false as stated, whenever a real Enriques surface with no real points exists. The paper treats that case as a genuine one, and such surfaces occur in the Degtyarev–Itenberg–Kharlamov classification. When S(R) is nonempty the item is right: [omega]_0 = 1, and the lifts delta_1, delta_2 = delta_1 + omega have [delta_i]_0 equal to the indicator functions of the two halves (one each, depending on labelling). So a nonzero class with [delta]_0 = 0 exists exactly when one half is all of S(R), and it is then unique. Fix, as the red team proposes: add 'S(R) nonempty' to item 118's hypotheses and record the omega/delta_i computation as its proof sketch. Nothing else changes. The [delta]_1 = cl_R(K_S) = w_1 clause is outside this finding (see /48). Medium severity is right.

Read item PAPER-BENOIST-19/15 and its consumers 21, 22 and 167, against printed pp. 64, 74-76, 79 and 104 (TeX (2.9)/can2, canZ, (2.16)/Brlift, proof of Theorem 0.5). The paper defines canonical decompositions, and so a degree-zero component, only for Z/2 coefficients (can2) and for rank-one integral sign systems L = Z(j) (canZ). No component is defined for Z/n(1) with n > 2. For alpha of period n, the paper takes a lift alpha~ in H^2_G(S(C), Z/n(1)) and says explicitly (p. 104) that its reduction xi mod 2 lifts (n/2)alpha, not alpha. I re-derived this. Reduction Z/n(1) -> Z/2 corresponds to mu_n -> mu_2, x -> x^{n/2}. This maps the n-Kummer sequence to the 2-Kummer sequence by x -> x^{n/2} on the middle G_m and the identity on the right. On H^2(G_m) the middle map is multiplication by n/2, so the image of xi in Br is (n/2)alpha. Evaluation into Br(R) = Z/2 is additive, so [xi]_0(x) = (n/2)·alpha|_x. That is 1_Theta when n ≡ 2 mod 4, and 0 when 4 | n even where Theta is nonempty. Such classes exist: if beta has period 4 and U(R) is connected and nonempty, one of beta and beta + (constant Hamilton class) has Theta = U(R) and still has period 4.
